title: Breathing Emergencies in Children: What the PCP Adds
next: Chapter 44, Lesson 3: Shock, rhythms, fever, seizures and infant death

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already give oxygen, bag, clear choking airways and give salbutamol. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Tell distress from failure before the child tires out
  2. Recognize croup, epiglottitis, asthma and bronchiolitis
  3. Use BC's pediatric doses for the PCP's breathing drugs

Textbook: Chapter 44, PDF pages 3745–3792
slides.say: Welcome back. Breathing problems are among the most common pediatric calls, and they matter even more in children, because most children who arrest get there through respiratory failure, not a heart problem. As EMRs, you already give oxygen, bag a child who isn't breathing well, clear a choking airway, and give salbutamol. Now that you're practising as a PCP, you add ipratropium, dexamethasone and intramuscular epinephrine, each with a child's dose and its own limits. Today we'll cover three things: distress versus failure, the classic childhood airway illnesses, and BC's pediatric doses for your breathing drugs.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。呼吸问题是最常见的儿科呼叫之一，而且对儿童更要紧，因为大多数心跳骤停的孩子是经由呼吸衰竭走到那一步的，而不是心脏问题。作为 EMR，你们已经会给氧、给呼吸不好的孩子做球囊通气、解除异物梗阻、给沙丁胺醇。现在以 PCP 身份执业，你多了异丙托溴铵、地塞米松和肌注肾上腺素，每种药都有儿童剂量和各自的限制。今天讲三件事：呼吸窘迫和呼吸衰竭的区别；儿童经典的气道疾病；以及 BC 给你这些呼吸药物规定的儿童剂量。

slides.title: Distress, failure, arrest
slides.body:
Distressworking harder, still exchanging gasretractions, flaring, grunting
Failurecompensation fails: low O₂, high CO₂sleepy, slowing, SpO₂ < 90% on O₂
Arrestno spontaneous breathingbag with oxygen now

Most pediatric cardiac arrests start as respiratory failure.
slides.say: Think of three stages on one road. In respiratory distress, the child works harder to breathe, and it works: gas exchange is still adequate. You'll see retractions, belly breathing, nasal flaring and grunting. In respiratory failure, the child can't keep it up, so oxygen falls or carbon dioxide builds up. This is decompensation, and it needs urgent oxygen and often ventilation. In respiratory arrest, the child isn't breathing, and you bag immediately with oxygen. Children rescued at the arrest stage often do well; once the heart stops too, the outcome is much worse. Your job is to catch the child early on this road.
slides.sayZh: 把它想成同一条路上的三个阶段。呼吸窘迫：孩子更用力地呼吸，而且有效，气体交换仍然足够；你会看到吸凹、腹式呼吸、鼻翼扇动和呻吟。呼吸衰竭：孩子撑不住了，氧下降或二氧化碳潴留，这是失代偿，需要紧急给氧，常常还要辅助通气。呼吸停止：孩子没有呼吸，立即用球囊加氧通气。在呼吸停止阶段被救回的孩子往往预后不错；一旦心跳也停了，结局就差得多。你的任务是在这条路上尽早截住孩子。

slides.title: Signs the child is tiring
slides.body:
CheckFailure looks like
Mental statusagitated, confused, sleepy (V, P or U)
Breathing ratefast → slow → stopped
Effortretractions fading, or severe with see-saw belly
Air entryquiet chest, diminished sounds
SpO₂under 90% on oxygen
Heart ratefast → slow

Sleepy + breathing hard = hypoxic until proven otherwise.
slides.say: How do you know the child is tiring? Watch the mental status first. An agitated, confused or sleepy child with breathing trouble is hypoxic until proven otherwise. The breathing rate goes from fast, to slow, to stopped, so a rate that's too slow for age is more worrying than one that's too fast. Retractions may fade simply because the muscles are exhausted, or become severe with a see-saw belly. A quiet chest with poor air entry is an ominous sign. A saturation under ninety percent despite oxygen means failure. And the heart rate goes from fast to slow; in a child, a slowing heart usually means hypoxia.
slides.sayZh: 怎么知道孩子在耗竭？先看神志。一个有呼吸困难、又烦躁、混乱或嗜睡的孩子，在排除之前都按缺氧处理。呼吸频率从快到慢再到停，所以比同龄正常值慢的呼吸比快的更让人担心。吸凹可能只是因为肌肉累垮而变浅，也可能变得很深、出现腹部跷跷板样矛盾运动。胸部安静、进气差是凶兆。给氧后血氧仍低于百分之九十就是衰竭。心率从快到慢；在孩子身上，心率变慢通常意味着缺氧。

slides.title: Choking: infant or child?
slides.body:
Infant (under 1 year)Child (over 1 year)
Can't cough, cry or speak5 back blows + 5 chest compressions, head downabdominal thrusts (BC also: back slaps, chest thrusts)
Becomes unresponsiveCPR; look in mouth before breathsCPR; look in mouth before breaths
  • Mild (coughing, pink): comfort, O₂, don't upset them
  • See it? Remove it. No blind finger sweeps
slides.say: Choking is common, because infants and toddlers put everything in their mouths: nuts, grapes, hot dogs, balloons and small toys. If the child can still cough and stays pink, it's a mild obstruction: position of comfort, oxygen if tolerated, don't upset them, and transport. If they can't cough or make a sound, act now. For an infant under one year, BC uses repeated cycles of five back blows and five chest compressions, with the head down. For an older child, use abdominal thrusts; BC also accepts back slaps and chest thrusts. If the child becomes unresponsive, start CPR, look in the mouth before each breath, and never do a blind finger sweep.
slides.sayZh: 异物梗阻很常见，因为婴幼儿什么都往嘴里塞：坚果、葡萄、热狗、气球和小玩具。孩子还能咳、肤色还好，就是轻度梗阻：舒适体位，能耐受就给氧，别惊扰他，转运。如果咳不出、发不出声音，立刻行动。一岁以下的婴儿，BC 规定反复做五次背部拍击加五次胸部按压，头朝下。大一些的孩子用腹部冲击；BC 也接受拍背和胸部冲击。孩子失去反应就开始 CPR，每次通气前先看口腔，绝不盲目用手指掏。

slides.title: Croup or epiglottitis?
slides.body:
CroupEpiglottitis
Causevirus, below the cordsbacteria, above the cords
Who6 months–6 years; fall, winterrare since Hib vaccine: ask about shots
Onsetdays of a cold; worse at nighthours: high fever, sore throat
Looksalert, barky cough, stridortoxic, drooling, sniffing position
Your movecalm; hypoxia = criticalhands off: no throat look, no IV
slides.say: Two upper airway infections behave very differently. Croup is a viral infection just below the vocal cords, the narrowest part of a child's airway. It's most common from six months to six years. The story is a few days of a cold, then a barky cough and stridor, worse at night. Most children stay alert and pink, so hypoxia or drowsiness means a critical obstruction. Epiglottitis is a bacterial infection above the cords, now rare thanks to the Hib vaccine, so ask about immunizations. It comes on within hours: high fever, sore throat, drooling, sitting in the sniffing position. Keep your hands off: don't look in the throat and don't start an IV.
slides.sayZh: 两种上气道感染表现大不相同。哮吼是声带正下方的病毒感染，那里正是儿童气道最窄的地方，多见于六个月到六岁。典型经过是先感冒几天，然后出现犬吠样咳嗽和喘鸣，夜间加重。多数孩子神志清楚、肤色红润，所以一旦缺氧或嗜睡，就是危重梗阻。会厌炎是声带上方的细菌感染，有了 Hib 疫苗之后已很少见，所以要问疫苗接种史。它几个小时内起病：高热、咽痛、流口水、坐成嗅物位。手别碰：不看喉咙，也不打静脉针。

slides.q: A 2-year-old with croup had stridor only when crying. Now she has stridor at rest, is drowsy, and her SpO₂ is falling. What does this mean?
options: She is calming down and getting better
Critical airway obstruction: support breathing, transport now
Normal for croup at night: give cool mist and wait
Likely asthma: give ipratropium on its own
slides.say: Question time. A two-year-old with croup had stridor only when she cried. Now she has stridor at rest, she's drowsy, and her oxygen saturation is falling. What does this mean? A, she is calming down and getting better. B, critical airway obstruction: support her breathing and transport now. C, normal for croup at night; give cool mist and wait. D, likely asthma; give ipratropium on its own. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来答题。一个两岁的哮吼患儿，原来只有哭的时候才有喘鸣，现在安静时也有喘鸣、变得嗜睡，血氧在往下掉。这说明什么？A，她在平静下来、正在好转；B，危重气道梗阻：支持呼吸，立即转运；C，哮吼夜里就是这样，给冷雾等着；D，可能是哮喘，单独给异丙托溴铵。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Hypoxia is uncommon in croup, so a falling saturation, stridor at rest and drowsiness mean severe swelling and a critical airway. Give oxygen, be ready to bag, since bag-mask ventilation often gets past the swelling, and move fast. A is the classic trap: a sleepy, hypoxic child is tiring, not settling. C wastes time, and the book calls cool mist controversial. D is wrong because this is an upper airway problem, and BC says ipratropium isn't used on its own.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。哮吼很少缺氧，所以血氧下降、静息喘鸣加上嗜睡，说明水肿严重、气道危重。给氧，准备好球囊面罩通气，因为球囊通气常能冲过肿胀处，并且要快。A 是典型陷阱：一个嗜睡、缺氧的孩子是在耗竭，不是在安静下来。C 浪费时间，而且书里说冷雾有争议。D 不对，这是上气道问题，而且 BC 规定异丙托溴铵不单独使用。

slides.title: Asthma in children
slides.body:
• Most common chronic illness of childhood
  • Spasm, mucus and swelling trap air going out
  • Mild–moderate: alert, sits up, wheezes breathing out
  • Severe: short phrases, wheeze in and out
  • Failing: drowsy, tripod, deep retractions, quiet chest

Ever in the ICU or intubated for asthma? High risk of a fatal attack.
slides.say: Asthma is the most common chronic illness of childhood. Three things narrow the small airways: muscle spasm, mucus and swelling, and they trap air going out. A child with a mild or moderate attack is alert, likes to sit up and wheezes on breathing out. As it gets worse, they speak in short phrases and wheeze in both directions. A failing child becomes drowsy, sits in a tripod, has deep retractions and may turn blue. If the wheeze disappears and air entry is poor, that's not improvement; it's a quiet chest. Ask about past ICU stays or intubation: those children are at high risk of a fatal attack.
slides.sayZh: 哮喘是儿童最常见的慢性病。三件事让小气道变窄：肌肉痉挛、黏液和肿胀，它们把呼出的气困在肺里。轻到中度发作的孩子神志清楚、喜欢坐着、呼气时有哮鸣。加重后说话只能说短句，吸气呼气都有哮鸣。衰竭的孩子变得嗜睡、取三脚架位、吸凹很深，可能发绀。如果哮鸣消失、进气又差，那不是好转，而是「安静胸」。要问以前有没有住过 ICU 或插过管：这样的孩子发生致命发作的风险很高。

slides.title: Bronchiolitis: the wheezy baby
slides.body:
• Viral swelling of the smallest airways, usually RSV
  • Under 2 years; late fall and winter
  • First wheeze under age 1? Think bronchiolitis, not asthma
  • Fast breathing, retractions, wheezes and crackles
  • Young infants may simply stop breathing (apnea)

Mostly supportive: comfort, O₂, gentle suction of nose and mouth.
slides.say: Bronchiolitis is a viral infection of the smallest airways, most often caused by RSV, respiratory syncytial virus. It affects children under two, mostly in late fall and winter. It can look like asthma, but asthma is rare under one year, so a baby's first wheezing episode in winter is probably bronchiolitis. You'll see fast breathing and retractions, and hear wheezes and crackles. Young infants may simply stop breathing for a while, called apnea. Care is mostly supportive: a position of comfort, often in the parent's arms, oxygen, and gentle suction of the nose and mouth. Drowsiness, severe retractions or a saturation under ninety percent means transport now.
slides.sayZh: 细支气管炎是最细小气道的病毒感染，最常见的病原是 RSV，也就是呼吸道合胞病毒。患儿在两岁以下，多发于深秋和冬季。它看起来可能像哮喘，但一岁以下哮喘很少见，所以婴儿冬天第一次喘，多半是细支气管炎。你会看到呼吸快、吸凹，听到哮鸣音和湿啰音。小婴儿可能只是一阵阵停止呼吸，也就是呼吸暂停。处理以支持为主：舒适体位（常常就在家长怀里）、给氧、轻柔吸引口鼻。一旦嗜睡、吸凹严重或血氧低于百分之九十，就立即转运。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: a child with asthma
slides.body:
BC protocol: shortness of breath with a history of asthma/COPD

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Position of comfort; limit movement
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%; auscultate
  • History and baseline vital signs
  • Salbutamol neb or MDI; transport after 1st dose
  • Flu-like illness: MDI with spacer

PCP adds

  • Add ipratropium (single dose)
  • IM epinephrine: SpO₂ < 90% and/or spasm unresolved
  • Consider dexamethasone
  • CPAP: not for age 12 and under
slides.say: Here's BC's protocol for shortness of breath with a history of asthma, applied to a child. The left column is what every licence level does: a position of comfort with little movement, oxygen aiming for ninety-four percent, listening to the chest, vitals, and salbutamol by nebulizer or inhaler, starting transport after the first dose. The right column is yours as a PCP: add ipratropium, as a single dose; give intramuscular epinephrine when the saturation stays under ninety percent or the spasm won't break; and consider dexamethasone. The protocol also lists CPAP, but BC's CPAP guideline excludes anyone aged twelve or under.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 针对有哮喘病史的呼吸困难的规程，用在孩子身上。左栏是所有执照级别都做的：舒适体位、少移动；给氧，目标九十四；听诊；生命体征；用雾化或吸入器给沙丁胺醇，给完第一剂就出发转运。右栏是你作为 PCP 的：加异丙托溴铵，只给一剂；血氧持续低于九十或痉挛解除不了时，肌注肾上腺素；考虑地塞米松。规程里也列了 CPAP，但 BC 的 CPAP 指引把十二岁及以下的患者全部排除。

slides.title: BC pediatric doses for breathing
slides.body:
DrugChild dose (BC)Limits
Salbutamol neb5 mg over age 1; 2.5 mg under 1repeat as required
Salbutamol MDI10–20 kg: 5 puffs; over 20 kg: 10 puffs (100 mcg)not under 10 kg; repeat up to 3 times
Ipratropium (PCP)250 mcg neb, or 80 mcg MDI (4 × 20)once; not under 30 days
Dexamethasone (PCP)0.5 mg/kg, max 16 mg; PO preferredcroup or asthma
Epinephrine0.01 mg/kg IM, max 0.5 mgIM only
slides.say: Here are BC's pediatric doses, which the exam uses. Salbutamol by nebulizer is five milligrams over age one, and two point five milligrams under one, repeated as required. By inhaler, it's not for children under ten kilograms; ten to twenty kilograms get five puffs of one hundred micrograms, over twenty kilograms get ten, and you may repeat up to three times. Ipratropium for a child is two hundred fifty micrograms by nebulizer, half a nebule, or four puffs, given once, and never under thirty days old. Dexamethasone is zero point five milligrams per kilogram, up to sixteen, preferably by mouth. Epinephrine is zero point zero one milligrams per kilogram IM, up to zero point five.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的儿童剂量，考试用的就是这些。沙丁胺醇雾化：一岁以上五毫克，一岁以下二点五毫克，按需重复。吸入器：十公斤以下不适用；十到二十公斤每疗程五喷、每喷一百微克，二十公斤以上十喷，最多可重复三次。异丙托溴铵儿童剂量是雾化二百五十微克，也就是半支，或吸入器四喷，只给一次，出生不满三十天的新生儿禁用。地塞米松每公斤零点五毫克，最多十六毫克，首选口服。肾上腺素每公斤零点零一毫克肌注，最多零点五毫克。

slides.q: A 6-year-old (22 kg) with asthma has had salbutamol and ipratropium. She is drowsy, air entry is poor, SpO₂ 87% on O₂. You're the PCP. Next step?
options: Repeat the ipratropium with the next salbutamol
Epinephrine 0.22 mg IM, keep giving salbutamol, transport
slides.say: A PCP decision. A six-year-old weighing twenty-two kilograms has asthma and has already had salbutamol and ipratropium. She's drowsy, air entry is poor, and her saturation is eighty-seven percent on oxygen. What's your next step? A, repeat the ipratropium with the next salbutamol. B, epinephrine zero point two two milligrams IM, keep giving salbutamol, and transport. C, start CPAP at five centimetres of water. D, epinephrine zero point five milligrams by IV push. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一个六岁、二十二公斤的哮喘患儿，已经用过沙丁胺醇和异丙托溴铵。她嗜睡，进气差，吸氧下血氧百分之八十七。下一步怎么做？A，下一剂沙丁胺醇里再加一次异丙托溴铵；B，肾上腺素零点二二毫克肌注，继续给沙丁胺醇，转运；C，以五厘米水柱开始 CPAP；D，肾上腺素零点五毫克静脉推注。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A saturation under ninety percent with unresolved bronchospasm is BC's trigger for IM epinephrine, and her dose is zero point zero one milligrams per kilogram: twenty-two kilograms gives zero point two two milligrams, under the zero point five maximum. Keep the salbutamol going and move. A is wrong because ipratropium is a single dose. C is wrong because CPAP is contraindicated at age twelve and under, and in a patient with a falling level of consciousness. D is wrong because on the BC licensing exam, epinephrine is IM only.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。血氧低于九十且支气管痉挛未解除，正是 BC 肌注肾上腺素的指征；她的剂量是每公斤零点零一毫克，二十二公斤就是零点二二毫克，低于零点五的上限。继续给沙丁胺醇并出发。A 错，异丙托溴铵只给一剂。C 错，十二岁及以下禁用 CPAP，意识下降的患者也禁用。D 错，BC 执照考试里肾上腺素只考肌注。

slides.title: Anaphylaxis in a child
slides.body:
• Epinephrine IM first, every licence level
  • Child: 0.01 mg/kg, max 0.5 mg; may repeat up to 3 times
  • PCP: IV + 20 mL/kg if still hypotensive or hypoperfused
  • PCP: salbutamol for wheeze after epinephrine
  • PCP: diphenhydramine, but not in neonates

Parent already used an auto-injector? Transport anyway: it wears off.
slides.say: In children, food is a leading trigger: nuts, eggs, milk and shellfish, sometimes hidden in daycare or school snacks. Epinephrine IM comes first, at every licence level: zero point zero one milligrams per kilogram, up to zero point five, and BC allows up to three repeats. As a PCP, you add an IV with twenty millilitres per kilogram if the child stays hypotensive or poorly perfused, and salbutamol for wheezing after the epinephrine. Diphenhydramine is also in your column, but it's contraindicated in newborns, and the BC monograph gives no weight-based child dose. If a parent already used an auto-injector and the child looks fine, transport anyway, because epinephrine wears off quickly.
slides.sayZh: 在孩子身上，食物是主要诱因：坚果、鸡蛋、牛奶和贝类，有时就藏在托儿所或学校的零食里。肾上腺素肌注永远第一，所有执照级别都给：每公斤零点零一毫克，最多零点五毫克，BC 允许最多重复三次。作为 PCP，如果孩子仍然低血压或灌注差，你加开静脉、按每公斤二十毫升补液；肾上腺素之后仍有哮鸣，就给沙丁胺醇。苯海拉明也在你这一栏，但新生儿禁用，而且 BC 药物专论没有按体重计算的儿童剂量。如果家长已经用过自动注射笔、孩子看起来没事，照样转运，因为肾上腺素作用消退得快。

slides.title: Airway and bagging a child
slides.body:
• Under 2: thin pad under the shoulders for a neutral airway
  • OPA: only with no gag reflex; mouth corner to jaw angle
  • NPA: rarely under 1; not with facial or significant head injury
  • Fighting the mask? Blow-by O₂, held by the parent
  • BVM: 1 breath every 2–3 s (book: 12–20/min), each about 1 s, just to chest rise
  • BC suction limits: 10 s child, 5 s infant
slides.say: Under age two, a thin pad under the shoulders keeps the airway neutral, because the back of the head is large. An oral airway is only for a child with no gag reflex; size it from the corner of the mouth to the angle of the jaw. A nasal airway is rarely used under one year, and not with facial trauma or a moderate to severe head injury. If a toddler fights the mask, let the parent hold blow-by oxygen. When you bag a child with a pulse, current heart-association guidance is one breath every two to three seconds; the book's older figure is twelve to twenty a minute. Give each breath over about one second, only until the chest rises. And BC limits suctioning to ten seconds in a child and five in an infant.
slides.sayZh: 两岁以下，在肩下垫一层薄垫，让气道保持中立位，因为孩子后脑勺大。口咽通气道只用于没有咽反射的孩子，尺寸从口角量到下颌角。鼻咽通气道一岁以下很少用，面部外伤或中重度颅脑外伤时不用。幼儿抗拒面罩，就让家长举着做吹氧。给有脉搏的孩子做球囊通气，现行心脏协会指南是每两到三秒一次；书里较旧的数字是每分钟十二到二十次。每次约一秒，胸廓一起伏就停。BC 规定吸引时间儿童不超过十秒，婴儿不超过五秒。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• CPAP is not for children 12 and under
  • Ipratropium: once only, not under 30 days, never alone
  • Salbutamol MDI: not under 10 kg (nebulizer dose instead)
  • Epinephrine (exam): IM only, max 0.5 mg: check your math
  • Croup, epiglottitis: no throat look, no IV, don't agitate
  • Bagging an asthmatic: slow rate, let the air out
slides.say: Here are the new traps at PCP level. CPAP is off the table for children twelve and under. Ipratropium is given once, never under thirty days of age, and never on its own. The salbutamol inhaler isn't indicated under ten kilograms; the nebulizer dose covers the smallest children. On the licensing exam, epinephrine is intramuscular only, with a maximum of zero point five milligrams, so double-check your weight-based math. With croup or epiglottitis, don't poke: no throat exam and no IV attempt. And if you must bag an asthmatic child, the book says use a slow rate and let each breath out, because trapped air can cause a pneumothorax.
slides.sayZh: 这些是 PCP 层面的新陷阱。十二岁及以下的孩子不能用 CPAP。异丙托溴铵只给一次，不满三十天禁用，也绝不单独用。沙丁胺醇吸入器十公斤以下不适用，最小的孩子用雾化剂量。执照考试里肾上腺素只考肌注，上限零点五毫克，所以按体重算完要再核一遍。哮吼或会厌炎别去捅：不看喉咙、不试静脉。如果不得不给哮喘孩子做球囊通气，书里说频率要慢、让每口气呼出去，因为困在肺里的气会造成气胸。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Croup, bronchiolitis: book uses nebulized epi; exam epi is IM only
  • Child IM epinephrine: book max 0.3 mg; BC max 0.5 mg
  • Ipratropium: book splits by weight; BC child 250 mcg neb / 80 mcg MDI
  • Salbutamol neb: book starts most young children at 2.5 mg; BC 5 mg over age 1
  • Book's atropine and needle decompression: not on the BC exam
slides.say: Where does the book differ from BC? For croup and bronchiolitis, the book uses nebulized epinephrine; on the licensing exam, epinephrine is IM only; BCEHS PCPs may nebulize it for croup after added-scope training. The book caps a child's IM epinephrine at zero point three milligrams; BC's maximum is zero point five. The book splits the ipratropium dose by weight, at ten kilograms; BC gives a child two hundred fifty micrograms by nebulizer or eighty micrograms by inhaler. The book starts most young children on two point five milligrams of nebulized salbutamol; BC gives five milligrams to every child over one year. And the book's atropine and chest needle decompression aren't on the exam; in BCEHS, needle decompression is an ACP skill.
slides.sayZh: 书和 BC 哪里不一样？哮吼和细支气管炎，书里用雾化肾上腺素；执照考试里肾上腺素只考肌注；BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1/2）培训后，可以给哮吼病人雾化肾上腺素。书里儿童肌注肾上腺素上限零点三毫克；BC 上限零点五。书里异丙托溴铵以十公斤为界按体重分剂量；BC 儿童一律雾化二百五十微克或吸入器八十微克。书里多数小孩子雾化沙丁胺醇从二点五毫克开始；BC 一岁以上都给五毫克。书里的阿托品和胸腔针刺减压都不在执照考试范围内；针刺减压在 BCEHS 属于 ACP 技能。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Sleepy + hard breathing, slowing rate or quiet chest = failure: act now
  2. Croup and epiglottitis: keep the child calm; hands off the throat
  3. BC child doses: epi 0.01 mg/kg IM (max 0.5), dexamethasone 0.5 mg/kg (max 16), ipratropium once

Next: shock, rhythms, fever, seizures and infant death
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: a child who is sleepy and breathing hard, whose rate is slowing, or whose chest has gone quiet, is in respiratory failure: oxygen, ventilation if needed, and go. Two: with croup or epiglottitis, keep the child calm, and keep your hands out of the throat. Three: know BC's pediatric doses: epinephrine zero point zero one milligrams per kilogram IM up to zero point five, dexamethasone zero point five milligrams per kilogram up to sixteen, and ipratropium given just once. Next lesson: shock, fever, seizures and sudden infant death. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，孩子嗜睡又呼吸费力、呼吸变慢、或胸部变安静，就是呼吸衰竭：给氧，需要时辅助通气，立刻出发。二，哮吼或会厌炎，让孩子保持平静，手别伸进喉咙。三，记住 BC 儿童剂量：肾上腺素每公斤零点零一毫克肌注、最多零点五；地塞米松每公斤零点五毫克、最多十六；异丙托溴铵只给一次。下节课讲休克、发热、抽搐和婴儿猝死。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
